why: Both analyses land on the key's hedgehog (profit per active relationship, not product count), the full stop-doing set (quotas, per-product pay, the eight-products goal, decentralized risk and HR) and all four brutal facts, so they are hard to separate on substance. Analysis 1 has the crisper verdict and a decline read closer to the key (Stage 1-2 with Stage 3 signs, the fine treated as a legacy matter, anomalies handled one termination at a time), while Analysis 2 is slightly better on calibration and on stating what would change its answer.
